prompt:
Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

Every category has a bidirectional nature. For example:

One person's sensitivity to the Care/Harm foundation may lead them to support high levels of immigration from poorer nations, to reduce the suffering of those who migrate. Whereas another person's sensitivity to the very same foundation may lead them to oppose those levels, because they believe it could lead to people they care about being harmed.

TEXT_E:
Britain forward, not back. New Labour’s 2005 manifesto applies enduring Labour values to a changing world with one core duty: government must provide opportunity and security for all. It seeks to embed a progressive consensus that rejects the old false choices between wealth creation and social justice, security and liberty, equal rights and protection from crime. The offer is investment plus reform; rights matched by responsibilities; services free to all, personal to each.

Record: macroeconomic stability, record employment, low inflation and mortgage rates; tax credits and a minimum wage that make work pay; real-terms investment transforming schools and the NHS; crime down 30%; poverty reduced for children and pensioners; stronger leadership in Europe; doubled aid and first-in-class action on climate through emissions trading.

Economy: entrench low debt and high employment under strict fiscal rules and a 2% inflation target; no rise in basic or top income tax rates, no VAT on essentials; redirect £21bn efficiencies to the frontline. Build an “opportunity economy” with skills, science (R&D to 2.5% of GDP by 2014), support for manufacturing and SMEs, fair procurement, lighter, smarter regulation, and competitive capital markets. Aim for 80% employment via New Deal, higher minimum wage, incapacity benefit reform, and personalised back-to-work support. Invest over £180bn in transport to 2015, with better rail, potential high-speed links, bus concessions, safety and low-carbon innovation, while exploring fair road pricing. Spread prosperity to every region; strengthen equality at work; back thriving rural economies and environmental stewardship.

Education: personalised learning and parental partnership from early years to HE. More teachers and support staff; primary basics plus arts, sport and languages; every secondary an independent specialist school, with fair admissions, strong discipline, and 200 Academies by 2010; Building Schools for the Future for modern facilities; stretch for the brightest and targeted catch-up. Transform 14–19 with high-quality vocational routes, specialised diplomas, apprenticeships and EMAs; reform FE; expand HE with fair, capped variable fees, bursaries and grants, and a 50% participation aim.

Crime and security: neighbourhood policing teams in every community; firm action on antisocial behaviour and alcohol-related disorder; tackle drugs with compulsory testing and treatment; create the Serious Organised Crime Agency; tougher penalties on guns and knives; cut reoffending with end-to-end offender management; strengthen victims’ rights. Managed migration that benefits Britain: a points-based system favouring skills, secure borders with biometrics and ID cards, faster, fairer asylum. Tackle terrorism with robust laws while upholding liberties.

NHS: free to all, personal to each; no charges for operations. Triple spending by 2008; cut referral-to-treatment waits to 18 weeks; expand capacity via NHS, independent and voluntary providers meeting NHS standards; extend patient choice; shift care to primary and community settings, including new community hospitals; drive cleanliness and clinical governance; focus on prevention—healthier school meals, food labelling, smoke-free workplaces and expanded cessation services.

Older people and families: maintain Pension Credit and universal benefits; build a cross-party pensions settlement that rewards saving; flexible retirement and work beyond 65; individual care budgets. End child poverty in a generation with tax credits, a Child Trust Fund, universal early years, 3,500 Sure Start Children’s Centres, extended schools 8–6, more paid maternity leave and flexible working; boost homeownership and renew social housing with more choice.

International: a leading Britain in a reformed EU; constitutional treaty by referendum; NATO at the core of defence; modern, well-equipped armed forces and a retained independent nuclear deterrent; support for democracy in Iraq and the Middle East; UN, World Bank and IMF reform. Global leadership on climate change (−20% CO2 by 2010, −60% by 2050) and on Africa (0.7% ODA by 2013, debt relief, fairer trade, universal access to AIDS treatment and basic services).

Quality of life and democracy: culture and sport for all (free museums, facilities, Olympic legacy); digital switchover; cleaner neighbourhoods, greener planning, a Marine Act. Devolution deepened; stronger, more accountable local government and neighbourhood powers; complete Lords reform; a Single Equality Act and a new Commission on Equality and Human Rights. The social contract remains clear: we help you; you help yourself; we all move forward together.

TEXT_D:
The Liberal Democrats’ Real Alternative is a costed, green, liberal programme built on Freedom, Fairness and Trust, with power devolved from Westminster and a strong internationalist outlook. A “green thread” runs throughout.

Fair, simple, affordable government
- Fully costed plans, switching around £5bn a year from low-priority spend (abolish unnecessary subsidies and the DTI’s wasteful functions; scrap ID cards; redirect the Child Trust Fund) to frontline priorities.
- One net tax rise: a 50% rate only on income over £100,000 to fund abolishing tuition and top-up fees, free personal care for the elderly and disabled, and lower local taxes.
- Replace the unfair Council Tax with a Local Income Tax based on ability to pay, saving the typical household about £450 a year; raise the stamp duty threshold to £150,000.

Putting patients first
- Free personal care for older and disabled people; more doctors, nurses and therapists; sweep away pointless central targets so clinicians and locally accountable bodies decide.
- Faster diagnosis via the quickest practical route; expand scans/tests (evenings/weekends), publish diagnostic waits.
- Free eye and dental checks; extend prescription charge exemptions; rebuild NHS dentistry; legislate for better mental health rights; ban smoking in enclosed public places; hardwire prevention and clean environments into health.

Ambitious for every child and learner
- Abolish tuition/top-up fees; restore fair grants; equalise college/school funding; modernise skills with a 14–19 diploma blending vocational and academic routes.
- Cut infant class sizes to an average of 20 (junior to 25) by hiring 21,000 teachers; extend wraparound care and complete 3,500 Children’s Centres.
- Less high-stakes testing; strengthen discipline and SEND support.

Tackling crime, defending liberty
- 10,000 more police by cancelling ID cards; cut red tape so officers patrol, not paperwork.
- Smart justice: tough community penalties for non-violent offenders; focus on traffickers and acquisitive crime.
- Repeal control-order regime; defend jury trial; prosecute terror in open courts (including intercept evidence); create a UK Border Force.
- Fair asylum decisions by a dedicated agency; allow asylum seekers to work; Single Equality Act and hate-crime units; specialist Environmental Tribunal.

Prosperity with less red tape, more green growth
- Independent budget scrutiny by the NAO; simpler, fairer business taxes; small-business rate relief; “sunset clauses” on regulation; duty to trade fairly; boost tourism.
- Green fiscal reform: shift to a Carbon Tax; incentives for efficient homes/clean vehicles; at least 20% electricity from renewables by 2020; do not replace ageing nuclear; promote hydrogen and clean tech.

Security, rights and global leadership
- Iraq was wrong; rebuild through the UN/EU, include Sunnis, strengthen Iraqi forces, and aim to withdraw UK troops with the UN mandate’s expiry.
- Support EU reform and the Constitution via referendum; prepare to join the euro when conditions are right; managed economic migration.
- Right-size procurement (cut Eurofighter Tranche 3) to fund troops’ welfare; retain a minimum nuclear deterrent while driving multilateral disarmament; tighten arms export controls.

Fair pensions and support
- Citizen’s Pension from 75 with earnings link (ending means-testing for around a million); Local Income Tax benefits eight in ten pensioners; £170/week Maternity Income Guarantee for six months; scrap the CSA and move enforcement to HMRC; extend Winter Fuel Payment to severely disabled adults; robust anti-fraud simplification.

Stronger local communities, rural fairness, better transport
- Devolve power, cut inspectorates to a streamlined Audit Commission; protect post offices and universal mail.
- Release public land to build 100,000 affordable homes; favour brownfield; control second homes where markets are distorted.
- Fair farm/food trading (Food Trade Inspector); CAP reform for public goods; Marine Act; Animal Welfare Commission; strict GM safeguards, promote organic.
- Fix rail with fewer, longer franchises and key upgrades; reward cleaner cars; expand congestion charging with upfront transit investment; plan national road-user charging to replace fuel/vehicle taxes; limit new roads; greener aviation taxes; free off-peak buses for pensioners/disabled and free railcards for target groups.

Better government
- Curb Prime Ministerial power (War Powers Act; Civil Service Act); predominantly elected second chamber; STV for all elections and votes at 16; deeper devolution; independent BBC regulator; Environmental Responsibility Act and a unified Environment–Transport–Energy department.

Climate leadership
- Beat UK Kyoto targets early; lead toward “contraction and convergence”; scale renewables, efficiency and recycling; help households cut bills and carbon.

Judge whether TEXT_E or TEXT_D aligns more closely with this profile, taking into account that each foundation may be invoked in either direction.

{
  "evidence": "<the specific commitments in each text you relied on>",
  "reasoning": "<two sentences connecting that evidence to the verdict>",

  "winner": "TEXT_E" | "TEXT_D"
}
